shared_context.topic: Taking NyQuil and Benadryl at the same time

snippets.output: Taking Nyquil and Benadryl at the same time for cold/flu symptoms is not recommended without consulting a healthcare professional.

Nyquil is an over-the-counter (OTC) medication that contains a combination of doxylamine (an antihistamine), dextromethorphan (a cough suppressant), and acetaminophen (a pain reliever and fever reducer).
snippets.pattern_notes: Definition + composition + each component's role: enumerated properties of one drug (Nyquil).

snippets.output: Benadryl is an antihistamine that contains diphenhydramine.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel facts about one drug: class + active ingredient.

snippets.output: Combining Nyquil and Benadryl can increase the risk of adverse effects, including drowsiness, dizziness, and confusion.
snippets.pattern_notes: General adverse-effect claim plus enumerated specifics.

snippets.output: Nyquil and Benadryl both have sedative properties, and taking Nyquil and Benadryl together can lead to excessive sedation.
snippets.pattern_notes: Causal chain: shared sedative properties (mechanism) -> excessive sedation (outcome).

snippets.output: Taking high doses of acetaminophen with other medications that contain acetaminophen can increase the risk of liver damage.

When taking Nyquil and Benadryl together, it is essential to follow the recommended dosage instructions for each medication and to consult a healthcare professional first; a healthcare professional can determine the best course of treatment and help ensure safety when taking Nyquil and Benadryl together.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated safety guidance (follow dosage, consult HCP) with reasons appended (HCP determines treatment, ensures safety). Primary A; secondary C since atoms 16-17 justify atom 15.
